builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Against Covert Misalignment
summary: Replaces single-pass chain-of-thought monitoring with a Bayesian trajectory monitor that fuses global context with local segment evidence, hardened against red-teamed trace-shaping attacks. Costs additional monitor inference over segmented traces plus integration and calibration effort, and likely depends on frontier API monitors (GPT-5.2, Claude-4.5) rather than a self-hosted 24 GB model. Can fail against adaptive evasions outside the TraceMRT attack distribution, and the 0.74 TPR at 5% FPR means roughly one in four covert trajectories is still missed.
rationale: CoT monitoring is a realistic safety layer for a small API-dependent team, but the demonstrated evasion success and residual miss rate mean the Bayesian monitor should be validated on the reader's own agent workloads before production reliance.
technique: Bayesian trajectory monitoring for covert CoT misalignment

claims.statement: Replaces single-pass chain-of-thought monitoring with a Bayesian trajectory monitor that fuses global context with local segment evidence, hardened against red-teamed trace-shaping attacks. Costs additional monitor inference over segmented traces plus integration and calibration effort, and likely depends on frontier API monitors (GPT-5.2, Claude-4.5) rather than a self-hosted 24 GB model. Can fail against adaptive evasions outside the TraceMRT attack distribution, and the 0.74 TPR at 5% FPR means roughly one in four covert trajectories is still missed.
Reports 0.91 AUC and 0.74 TPR at FPR=0.05 against trace-shaped evasion attacks; no multiplicative factor is stated.
